title: Karate Champ
description: Karate Champ arrived in arcades in 1984 as one of the earliest one-on-one karate games, where two martial artists face off in a series of bouts scored by clean hits, using an unusual twin-stick control scheme for punches and kicks. Its cabinets drew crowds who watched strangers learn matchups, trade strategies between rounds, and settle rivalries one bout at a time.
body:
Karate Champ arrived in arcades in 1984 as one of the earliest one-on-one karate games, where two martial artists face off in a series of bouts scored by clean hits, using an unusual twin-stick control scheme for punches and kicks. Its cabinets drew crowds who watched strangers learn matchups, trade strategies between rounds, and settle rivalries one bout at a time.

This tribute demo recreates the back-and-forth of a bout in text form: you pick jab, hook, kick, special, or block each round while a computer opponent cycles through its own pattern of moves. It is an original miniature inspired by the mechanics of Karate Champ, not a copy of that game, and it uses none of its art, music, or code.

A good habit in this style of bout is to block when the opponent presses forward, then answer with a quick jab rather than a slow heavy attack.
controls: Type jab, hook, kick, special or block each round, or quit to stop.

body:
Marvel vs. Capcom arrived in arcades in 1998 as a tag-team crossover fighter that pairs comic-book heroes with video-game fighters, built on fast assists, air combos, and screen-filling hyper combos. Its cabinets drew crowds who watched strangers learn matchups, trade strategies between rounds, and settle rivalries one bout at a time.

This tribute demo recreates the back-and-forth of a bout in text form: you pick jab, hook, kick, special, or block each round while a computer opponent cycles through its own pattern of moves. It is an original miniature inspired by the mechanics of Marvel vs. Capcom, not a copy of that game, and it uses none of its art, music, or code.

Watching the opponent's pattern matters more than speed: a fighter who always blocks after two attacks can be caught with a delayed hook.
controls: Type jab, hook, kick, special or block each round, or quit to stop.
